name: virtual event streaming platforms for hybrid events
title: Best Virtual Event Streaming Platforms for Hybrid Events in 2026
summary_line: Hybrid event platforms join an onsite audience and remote viewers in one program, with registration, streaming, sessions, sponsors and attendee data.
definition: A virtual event streaming platform for hybrid events runs a program that people attend in a venue and online at once. It streams the sessions, handles registration and agendas, and usually adds chat, Q&A, networking, sponsor booths and reports so organizers can see who watched what.
intro: A hybrid event fails in a particular way: the room gets the production budget and the remote audience gets a camera on a tripod. Multi-day conferences and game showcases need both groups to register once, watch the same sessions and reach sponsors in the same place. We compared ten platforms by reading each vendor's own pages: product descriptions, pricing pages, plan structure, supported formats and company details. We did not run an event on any of them, and claims such as customer counts or analyst rankings are marked as the vendor's. Weight went to tools that document both halves of a hybrid program, show a price or a clear route to one, and say how remote viewers take part rather than just watch.

criteria.heading: Which half of the event it covers
criteria.text: Cvent, Accelevents, vFairs and Bizzabo document venue-side tools such as check-in, badge printing and mobile apps. Vimeo and Zoom Events and Webinars concentrate on the stream. Virtual PRO and Airmeet sit in between with booths, lounges and networking. Decide whether your weak point is the room or the broadcast, then choose a platform that is strongest where you are thinnest.

criteria.heading: Audience limits and program length
criteria.text: Virtual PRO publishes audience caps per event, from 1,000 to 40,000 across four plans, while Zoom's Webinars plan covers up to 500 attendees. Most others give no cap in the pages we read. For a multi-day showcase, check concurrent viewers, the number of parallel channels, and whether the plan allows unlimited events or sells them one at a time.

criteria.heading: Price transparency and contract shape
criteria.text: Only Accelevents ($7,500 per event or from $13,500 a year) and Virtual PRO ($15,000 to $125,000 a year) print dollar figures. The rest sell through demos. A per-event license suits a one-off showcase; an annual one suits a calendar. Ask whether seats, attendees or events drive the price, because each rewards a different program.

criteria.heading: What happens to sponsors and data
criteria.text: Sponsors fund most hybrid programs. Bizzabo lists sponsor ROI, vFairs a lead capture app, Swapcard exhibitor analytics and Airmeet attendee analytics. Check that both onsite and online visits land in one report and sync to your CRM; Virtual PRO names HubSpot, Salesforce and Marketo for that.

market_notes: Of ten platforms, only two publish dollar prices on the pages we read: Accelevents and Virtual PRO. Zoom lists three plan names without amounts, and the other seven offer a demo, a quote or a link to a pricing page we did not open. Free trials or free plans are mentioned for Goldcast, Airmeet, Cvent, Accelevents and Vimeo. Three vendors state United States addresses (Airmeet, Cvent, Virtual PRO), and none of the ten states a European base in the pages opened.

The trade-off is breadth against depth. Suites such as Cvent and Bizzabo cover registration, venue and sponsors but describe streaming as one feature; video-first products such as Vimeo and Zoom stream well but leave registration and exhibitors to others. One naming wrinkle: the web address of Hubilo, a long-standing name in this market, now opens Virtual PRO from Brandlive, so older write-ups may describe a product that has since moved.

how_to_choose.title: Map the program before the tool
how_to_choose.text: Write the agenda: how many days, parallel tracks, speakers in the room versus remote, sponsor slots. A one-day reveal with a single stage needs a stream and registration; a three-day show with booths needs exhibitors, lounges and meetings. This map decides whether to shortlist suites like Cvent and Accelevents or video-first options like Vimeo and Zoom.

how_to_choose.title: Ask for the price in your event shape
how_to_choose.text: Request a quote for your attendee count, number of events a year and admin seats. Compare Accelevents' per-event model with Virtual PRO's annual tiers, and ask the quote-only vendors to separate platform, production services and support. Insist on knowing what an extra event or an audience over the cap costs.

how_to_choose.title: Test the remote experience as an attendee
how_to_choose.text: Have a colleague who is not an organizer register, join from a phone and try Q&A, a booth visit and replay. Remote viewers are lost in the first minutes if login, audio or captions fail. Virtual PRO and Zoom list AI captions; confirm languages and accessibility for your audience before signing.

faqs.q: What is the best virtual event streaming platform for hybrid events in 2026?
faqs.a: Cvent is our first pick for large hybrid programs because it covers venue, registration, virtual experience and webinars in one vendor. Accelevents is better when you need a published price, and Virtual PRO when you run many multi-day events a year and want audience caps and booths spelled out.

faqs.q: How much does a hybrid event platform cost?
faqs.a: Few publish prices. Accelevents lists $7,500 per event or from $13,500 a year for unlimited events, and Virtual PRO lists $15,000, $50,000 and $125,000 a year across three tiers. Cvent, Goldcast, Airmeet, vFairs and others require a demo or quote.

faqs.q: Can one platform handle both the venue and the stream?
faqs.a: Cvent, Accelevents, vFairs and Bizzabo describe onsite tools such as check-in, badging and mobile apps alongside virtual features. Vimeo and Zoom describe the stream only, so a venue workflow would need a second system.

faqs.q: Do these platforms support sponsor booths?
faqs.a: Several do. Virtual PRO lists sponsors, exhibitors, booths and lounges, Airmeet lists exhibition booths, Swapcard exhibitor management and ROI analytics, and vFairs a floor plan builder with a lead capture app. Check how leads reach your CRM.

faqs.q: Is Zoom enough for a hybrid conference?
faqs.a: For a single-stage event with a few hundred viewers, often yes. Zoom's Webinars plan covers up to 500 attendees with polls, Q&A and AI captions. For multi-day programs with booths, sponsors and onsite check-in, a dedicated event platform is a better fit.

Its former web address now opens Virtual PRO, an enterprise virtual and hybrid event platform from Brandlive, according to the company page. We list Virtual PRO on the facts we could read and do not assume any earlier Hubilo terms still apply.

faqs.q: How should I prepare a game showcase as a hybrid event?
faqs.a: Keep one registration for both audiences, rehearse the stream with the real speakers, and decide how remote viewers ask questions. Plan a replay page and clips afterward, since Goldcast and Airmeet both describe tools for repurposing recordings.

tools.name: Cvent
tools.tagline: Event platform spanning registration, venues, hybrid and webinars
tools.best_for: Large programs mixing in-person and online
tools.pricing: No prices on the opened home page; it points to a separate pricing page. The home page offers a free trial of Cvent event registration.
tools.platforms: Event mobile apps; virtual experience platform; webinars; check-in and badging
tools.summary: Covers the physical half of a hybrid event as thoroughly as the streamed half, which few rivals here do.
tools.verdict: A hybrid conference has two audiences and one budget, and Cvent is the entry that plans both. It handles venue sourcing, hotel room blocks, check-in and badging for the room, then adds a virtual experience platform and webinars for remote attendees. The vendor says 89% of the Fortune 100 use it, with 34K+ customers and over 10M events managed, though those are its own claims. A multi-day showcase with sponsors, travel and badge printing gains most from having the venue and stream records in one system.
tools.weaknesses: No price is printed on the page we opened, so budgeting needs a sales call. The breadth is also the drawback: a team that only wants a polished stream may pay for venue and hotel modules it never opens.
tools.wrong_for: A video-first marketing team that wants quick webinars should look at Goldcast or Zoom Events and Webinars.

sources.fact: Cvent describes its product as an event platform for in-person, virtual and hybrid events and webinars.
The home page offers a free trial of Cvent event registration and shows no prices.
The home page gives a Tysons Corner, Virginia address (1765 Greensboro Station Place, 7th Floor).

tools.name: Accelevents
tools.tagline: Event platform with published per-event and annual pricing
tools.best_for: Teams that need a budget figure up front
tools.pricing: Professional $7,500 per event (one event); Business from $13,500 per year for unlimited events; Enterprise and White Label are custom priced.
tools.platforms: Web platform; event mobile app; onsite check-in and badge printing
tools.summary: One of two platforms in this group that print dollar figures, which makes budgeting for a hybrid program unusually concrete.
tools.verdict: Accelevents is placed second because a planner can price it from the page alone. A single event costs $7,500 on the Professional plan, and a producer running a spring showcase, a summer summit and a winter conference can compare that with $13,500 or more per year for unlimited events on Business. Registration, check-in, badge printing and an agenda builder serve the room, while a virtual event hub serves remote guests. The vendor says its customers include Fortune 500 companies, associations and independent show organizers.
tools.weaknesses: The entry price is high for a small studio streaming a single reveal, and the Business figure is a floor labeled from $13,500 rather than a fixed price. Enterprise and White Label need a quote. A free trial exists, but its length is not stated in the text we read.
tools.wrong_for: An indie team with a small budget and one livestream should use Vimeo or Zoom Events and Webinars rather than paying per event.

sources.fact: Accelevents is an event management platform covering registration, check-in, agendas, virtual event hubs and attendee engagement.
Accelevents' Professional plan costs $7,500 per event for one event, and its Business plan starts at $13,500 per year for unlimited events.
Accelevents' Enterprise and White Label plans are custom priced.
Accelevents states that its customers include Fortune 500 companies, associations, independent show organizers and others.

tools.name: Virtual PRO
tools.tagline: Multi-day virtual and hybrid platform with greenroom and sponsor booths
tools.best_for: Conference producers with a steady event calendar
tools.pricing: Annual plans: PRO 1 $15,000 per year, PRO 4 $50,000, PRO 10 $125,000, PRO max by quote; every plan allows unlimited events, with pricing scaled to admin seats.
tools.platforms: Web platform; HD streaming with adaptive bitrates
tools.summary: Aimed squarely at producers of multi-session, multi-day programs, with audience caps and prices spelled out.
tools.verdict: Virtual PRO describes itself as built for multi-session, multi-day events, and its pricing page backs that with specifics: unlimited events on every plan, a per-event audience cap from 1,000 to 40,000, and seat counts from one admin to unlimited. A showcase team with a greenroom for speakers, sponsor booths, lounges and breakout meetings has the pieces in one place. Real-time CRM integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce and Marketo are listed on the homepage, according to the vendor.
tools.weaknesses: There is no free plan, and the entry plan costs $15,000 a year with one admin seat and one channel, so it only pays off for a producer with several events a year. The address that once led to Hubilo now opens this product, so buyers should not assume old Hubilo terms apply.
tools.wrong_for: A team running one conference should prefer Accelevents' per-event plan or a Zoom Events license.

sources.fact: The pricing page lists PRO 1 at $15,000 per year, PRO 4 at $50,000 per year and PRO 10 at $125,000 per year, with PRO max through sales; every plan has unlimited events.
Audience caps per event are 1,000 on PRO 1, 4,000 on PRO 4, 10,000 on PRO 10 and 40,000 on PRO max.
The company page says Virtual PRO is built by Brandlive and gives a Portland, Oregon address under Brandlive, Inc.
The homepage lists HD streaming with adaptive bitrates, multilingual captions and real-time CRM integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce and Marketo.

tools.name: Airmeet
tools.tagline: Browser event and studio platform with networking and exhibition booths
tools.pricing: No prices or plan names on the opened home page; a Start Your Free Trial link is offered and a separate pricing page exists but was not opened.
tools.platforms: Browser-based; multi-platform live streaming; event hosting and embeds
tools.summary: Strong on attendee-to-attendee interaction, with a recording studio and AI clips attached.
tools.verdict: Airmeet focuses on the audience side of a hybrid event: networking, exhibition booths and attendee analytics (the vendor calls it X-ray) sit beside webinars and hybrid sessions. Its Airstudio product records, streams and produces from the browser, and Airshots generates AI clips from the recordings, so a multi-day show leaves reusable video behind. The home page lists logos from Kaiser Permanente, Comcast, Capgemini, ADP and Cognizant and claims more than 4,000 organizations, as the vendor's own figures. A free trial is offered.
tools.weaknesses: Pricing and plan names are absent from the page we opened, so cost is unknown. The page gives a California address, but its structured data also lists one in Bangalore, India, which makes the legal setup less clear than a single entity statement would.
tools.wrong_for: Teams wanting a venue, hotel and badge workflow around the stream should choose Cvent instead.

sources.fact: Airmeet Inc. is named as the legal entity on the vendor site.
Airmeet describes itself as 'THE AI POWERED VIDEO PLATFORM', combining live events, recording, streaming, podcasts and AI video tools.
The home page offers a 'Start Your Free Trial' link and shows no prices.
The home page lists the address 440 N Barranca Ave, Covina, California 91723, United States.

tools.name: Goldcast
tools.tagline: AI-first B2B video platform for webinars, events and content reuse
tools.best_for: Marketing teams turning events into video
tools.pricing: Quote only: plans are custom bundles; the pricing page offers a demo request and a free trial.
tools.summary: Treats the live event as raw material for clips and content, which suits B2B marketers more than venue planners.
tools.verdict: Goldcast calls itself an AI-first video content platform for B2B, covering webinars, virtual and hybrid events and podcasts. The product list includes Goldcast Events, Content Lab for repurposing and a Recording Studio, so a hybrid keynote can become a library of clips. Enterprise plans add team workspaces, SSO, custom reports, custom permissions and multi-language support. The vendor cites a 2026 B2B webinar benchmark report on its site, a sign that its focus is demand generation.
tools.weaknesses: No price is published and plans are custom bundles, so you have to book a demo to learn the cost. The pages we read say little about in-person tools such as check-in or badging, so the physical half of a hybrid event may need another system.
tools.wrong_for: A planner who needs onsite check-in and badge printing should look at Accelevents, vFairs or Cvent.

sources.fact: Goldcast describes itself as an AI-first video content platform for B2B videos, webinars and events.
Goldcast's pricing page offers a free trial and asks visitors to get a demo for custom bundles, so pricing is not published.
Goldcast's enterprise offer includes team workspaces, SSO, custom reports, custom permissions and multi-language support.
Goldcast's copyright notice names Goldcast, Inc.

tools.name: vFairs
tools.tagline: Registration, ticketing, mobile app and floor plans for all event formats
tools.pricing: Pricing not shown on the opened page; the page asks visitors to request pricing or a free guided demo.
tools.platforms: Web platform; mobile event app; onsite badge printing
tools.summary: A full event-management suite that fits trade-show style hybrid programs with a floor plan and lead scanning.
tools.verdict: vFairs bundles registration, ticketing, a mobile app and a floor plan builder with a lead capture app, which matches a hybrid exhibition where sponsors want scanned leads and a booth map. It covers in-person, hybrid and virtual formats under one roof. The vendor states it was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Event Marketing and Management Platforms for the second year in a row, a third-party ranking we did not verify.
tools.weaknesses: The pricing page lists no figures and offers only a pricing request or a free guided demo, so cost and any trial terms are unknown. The pages we read give no company or headquarters details.
tools.wrong_for: A producer who mainly wants polished streaming and a greenroom should compare Virtual PRO before choosing a suite like this.

sources.fact: vFairs is an event management platform for in-person, hybrid and virtual events, covering registration, ticketing, mobile apps and check-in.
vFairs' pricing page asks visitors to request pricing information or a free guided demo rather than listing prices.
vFairs states that it was named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Event Marketing and Management Platforms for the second consecutive year.

tools.name: Bizzabo
tools.tagline: Event Experience OS with mobile app, networking and SmartBadges
tools.best_for: B2B event leaders tracking sponsor return
tools.pricing: No prices or plan names on the opened home page; navigation links to a pricing page that was not opened. No free plan or trial is mentioned.
tools.platforms: Mobile event app; onsite software and wearables; web event pages
tools.summary: Good for measuring sponsor value across a program, with onsite badges and a mobile app for the room.
tools.verdict: Bizzabo describes its product as the Event Experience OS for B2B event leaders and lists registration, an agenda editor, a mobile event app, networking and sponsor ROI reporting. Klik SmartBadges are wearables that give onsite data, which is rare among the tools here. Video, broadcasting and streaming appear among its features, so the remote audience is covered, though streaming is one item among many. Its home page shows logos from Amazon, Bloomberg and others without calling them customers, and names Phenom and Inductive Automation in stories.
tools.weaknesses: The home page shows no prices and no trial, only a demo. Streaming is listed as a feature but described in less detail than registration and onsite tools, so a showcase that depends on production quality needs a closer look.
tools.wrong_for: A team that wants a webinar-first workflow with content repurposing should use Goldcast or Airmeet.

sources.fact: Bizzabo sells its platform as the 'Event Experience OS' for B2B event leaders.
The home page links to a pricing page, but shows no prices or plan names.
The home page offers a demo and does not mention a free plan or trial.
The home page lists event registration, a mobile event app, event networking, sponsor ROI and Klik SmartBadges among its features.

tools.name: Swapcard
tools.tagline: Event app and AI matchmaking for registration and exhibitors
tools.pricing: Not stated on the opened home page; no pricing page URL was found in the page content, and no trial is mentioned.
tools.summary: Leans on matchmaking and the event app; streaming details are thin in what we could read.
tools.verdict: Swapcard pitches a single platform for registration, the event app, exhibitor tools and AI matchmaking, with onsite services and check-in for the physical side. The meta description says it is top rated for ease of use and support on G2, and the home page claims twice the industry average app adoption, both vendor statements. For a conference where meeting the right people matters more than the keynote, the matchmaking and exhibitor analytics are the point.
tools.weaknesses: The pages we read do not mention live video features, a free plan, a trial or prices, so it is the hardest tool here to judge as a streaming platform. No customers are named on the home page.
tools.wrong_for: A showcase that depends on broadcast-grade streaming should choose Virtual PRO or Vimeo, which describe streaming directly.

sources.fact: Swapcard describes itself as one event management platform for registration, the event app, exhibitor tools and AI matchmaking.
The home page does not state pricing, a free plan or a trial.
The meta description on the home page says the platform is 'Top rated for ease of use and support on G2'.

tools.name: Zoom Events and Webinars
tools.tagline: Zoom's one-to-many webinar and event platform with three plans
tools.pricing: Three plans are listed (Webinars, Webinars Plus, Events); dollar amounts are not on the page and the vendor refers to a separate events pricing page. Webinars is for up to 500 attendees.
tools.summary: Familiar to attendees and easy to adopt, but light on the exhibition and venue side of a hybrid event.
tools.verdict: Zoom Events and Webinars suits a company whose staff and guests already live in Zoom. The page describes one-to-many presentations from simple sessions to full broadcasts, with branding, production tools and analytics, and lists Simulive, a Production Studio, breakout rooms, polls and Q&A, AI captions and CRM integrations. Three tiers let a team start at a 500-attendee Webinars plan and move to Events for bigger programs. For a half-day hybrid product reveal, that familiarity shortens training.
tools.weaknesses: Dollar prices are not on the page we opened, and the page does not mention onsite tools such as check-in or exhibitor floor plans, so it works better for the broadcast than for the venue.
tools.wrong_for: A multi-day trade show with booths and sponsors should look at Virtual PRO, vFairs or Accelevents.

sources.fact: Zoom Webinars is described as a platform for one-to-many presentations, from simple sessions to full broadcasts, with branding, production tools and analytics.
The page lists three plans: Webinars (up to 500 attendees), Webinars Plus (adds AI, on-demand video and pro production tools) and Events.
Dollar prices are not shown on the page; the vendor refers to a separate events pricing page for current rates.
The copyright notice on the page names Zoom Communications, Inc.

tools.name: Vimeo
tools.tagline: Video hosting with live streaming, webinars and OTT
tools.best_for: Studios that already host video there
tools.pricing: Free plan with Start for free; paid plans from the upgrade page; enterprise via Contact sales. No prices appear in the text of the pages opened.
tools.platforms: Browser and mobile app; live streaming; webinars; OTT
tools.summary: A video host first and an event platform second, useful for streaming a keynote and keeping the replay.
tools.verdict: Vimeo covers the video layer of a hybrid event: live streaming, webinars, a player, an editor and on-demand sales, with a free plan to begin. A game studio running a showcase can stream the keynote, host the replay and sell access through Vimeo On Demand or OTT, all in one account. The homepage claims 287 million creatives, entrepreneurs and businesses trust the service, a figure that is the vendor's own, and the footer names Vimeo.com, Inc.
tools.weaknesses: It offers no event registration suite, exhibitor booths or networking in the pages we read, so a multi-day conference needs extra tools. Prices are not in the opened text.
tools.wrong_for: A conference with sponsors and booths should use Virtual PRO or Accelevents instead of assembling pieces around a video host.

sources.fact: Vimeo describes itself as an all-in-one video platform for creating, managing and sharing video.
The Vimeo homepage offers a Start for free option, and its upgrade page describes plans from free to enterprise.
The Vimeo homepage lists webinars, live streaming, Vimeo OTT and Vimeo On Demand among its products.
The Vimeo site footer reads 2026 Vimeo.com, Inc.
